fixes.explanation: Souls under an altar do appear earlier in Revelation (Revelation 6:9). That's earlier in the book, though, and this is a different scene. In this passage John says something else about these ones. "…they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years."

John never says the saints march out. He only says the army surrounds the camp of the saints and the beloved city. The next thing he reports is the fire. "But fire came down from heaven and consumed them."

That's the one, friend. The angel had the key to the Abyss, and John says he "…threw him into the Abyss, shut it, and sealed it over him…" Key, chain, shut, sealed. That angel did not leave one detail to chance.

Yes, baker. John says the angel sealed the Abyss over him "…so that he could not deceive the nations until the thousand years were complete." Deceiving the nations is what he can't do while he's sealed in there. Until the thousand years are complete, that's off the table.
That's it. John sees the souls of those beheaded "…for their testimony of Jesus and for the word of God…" Their testimony was about Jesus, and it cost them. Jesus is named right there in the verse.

Moses was Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), and he's a big name in Scripture. John doesn't name him here, though. The text says these people were beheaded "…for their testimony of Jesus and for the word of God."
Elijah was a prophet (1 Kings 18:36), and he's a big name too. But John doesn't mention him in this vision. These souls were beheaded "…for their testimony of Jesus and for the word of God."
Harvest is a fine word, but John doesn't use it here. Verse 5 says, "This is the first resurrection." That's the word that fits the blank, straight from John.
John doesn't say the army turns around. After they surround the camp and the city, he says, "But fire came down from heaven and consumed them." That's what he reports happening to them.

That's right, baker. John writes, "…if anyone was found whose name was not written in the Book of Life, he was thrown into the lake of fire." Anyone whose name isn't found in that book is the one thrown in. I think it's a sobering way to end the passage.
